summary: Verify or refute audit finding S1-21 (identity windows in user twin VA spaces) from source; explain why apps pass

result.answer:
**Short answer.** You're right about the part of v3 the apps use, and the audit is right about a second part. A twin's host VA space holds two kinds of mapping:

- **Guest rows.** These are exactly the leaves the guest's own page tables state, mapped FIXED at the guest's own addresses. Privileged leaves are withheld from user twins. This is the "only map what's needed" part, and it is what the 61 passing apps run on. [READ c1, c2]
- **Two windows that kayfabe adds.** One maps the whole store (all guest VRAM, including the guest kernel's GPU page tables and kayfabe's own BAR1/BAR2 roots). The other maps all guest RAM. No guest page-table entry asks for either. [READ c3, c4]

**1. Scope.** `create_mirror` maps both windows into every mirror, with no user/kernel branch. Prewarmed spares get them too, and recycled spares keep them. [READ c3] Passthrough twins are born in that same mirror space. [READ c5] The store window is in every twin with no exception, because a mirror is only recorded once the store window has mapped. The RAM window is in every twin unless the guest-RAM object failed. [READ c6] I confirmed this on hardware: guest-USER twins (`privilege=0`) were born in a space logged with both windows. [MEASURED c7]

**2. Why 61 apps pass.** Passthrough work is never parsed and never uses a window address. The only thing that reads window addresses is the Translated rewriter for the guest kernel's copy-engine work. [READ c8] The windows sit at the top of the space, where no guest row lives, and no guest leaf ever collided with one. [READ c9; MEASURED c10] Passing apps show that the needed mappings are present. They cannot show that extra mappings are absent. In the 61/65 run itself, deviceQuery's user mirror had both windows and it passed. [MEASURED c10] Every app in that run also ran as guest root (`privilege=1`), so the matrix never tested an unprivileged user. [MEASURED c10] So the code does "only map what's needed" for rows, but not for windows.

**3. Why the windows exist.** The design rule §12 (commit `8ecad812`, 2026-09-22) says the window must not live in a separate VA space used only for Translated work. The reason: the guest's unified-memory driver (UVM) mixes physical and virtual addresses in one command stream, so the window has to sit beside the guest rows. The rule then says "every host VAS we create". [READ c11] The history after that:
- P5 (`09252909`, 09-25) built the windows into every mirror.
- P5b (`90784294`, 53 minutes later) put user channels into those same mirrors.
- v3-roperm (`efce970b`, 09-26) withheld privileged rows from user twins but left the windows alone.

A mirror's kernel/user status isn't known when it is built: UVM's space only becomes kernel at its first Translated birth. [READ c12] So putting windows everywhere was a convenience, not something the apps need. Section §24.2 of the design doc says the windows are "in Translated spaces"; the code doesn't match that. [READ c11]

**4. Read or measured.** The access property is only READ from source. `map_window` adds only `GROWS_DOWN` and `CACHE_SNOOP`, so the mappings are read-write. On RM's NVOS46 path the privilege bit starts at zero and is never set, so the PTEs are non-privileged. [READ c13, c14] That means P0 (twin channels born as USER) does not shrink the exposure. Whether the hardware enforces anything beyond the PTE is UNVERIFIED. The test that would settle it is **T-WINDOW-USER**, with a `windows=none` census on user mirrors. It has never run, and no trace on any origin branch mentions it. [READ c15]

**5. Where the audit overstates.** The substance holds. Three fixes:
- Its line pointer is stale (see c3).
- "passes no privileged flag" points at a flag that doesn't exist (c13).
- "reachable" is read from source, not measured.

Corrected sentence: *"Every mirrored host space, including guest user processes' twin spaces, carries a read-write, non-privileged map of the whole store and all guest RAM, placed whether the space is user or kernel; reachability from user work is READ and T-WINDOW-USER has not run; it stays inside the VM."*

**6. Fix.** P1/P2 creates one Translated-only VA space per VM that holds both windows and kayfabe's rings. Guest twins then hold only guest rows (design §4, rollout step 3 `KF3_TSPACE=1`). On the data path, passthrough apps should be unaffected. [READ c8; the A/B run is UNVERIFIED] One catch: today a mirror whose windows fail is never recorded, so every birth is refused with "has no mirror", passthrough included. P1 has to separate the mirror record from the windows; the comment at `mem.rs:1786-1788` understates this. [READ c6] It also saves 0.3–0.9 s per new mirror. [MEASURED c7, c10]

result.summary:
ANSWER TO THE OWNER: both statements are true, about two different layers of the same host VA space. At kayfabe origin/master e4fb0190, every host twin space holds two things.

(a) Mirrored rows: exactly the leaves the guest's own page tables state, placed FIXED at the guest's VAs as slices of the store or guest-RAM object. Privileged leaves are withheld in user twins. This is the "only map what's needed" layer, it is what every passthrough app actually uses, and it is why 61/65 passes.

(b) Two kayfabe-owned whole-object aliases ("windows"): all of the store (all guest VRAM, including the firmware carve-out that holds kayfabe's own BAR1/BAR2 root pages) and all guest RAM. They are mapped read-write and non-privileged, GROWS_DOWN, at the top of the space, at VAs no guest PTE names.

Only Translated channels (guest-kernel CE: CeUtils and UVM) dereference the windows. No passthrough path reads them. The 61/65 binary (2830988f) already had windows in every user twin, with window code byte-identical to master. So the matrix shows the needed rows are present. It cannot show the unneeded windows are absent, and it is no evidence for or against S1-21.

Why they are everywhere: THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE §12 (8ecad812, 2026-09-22) ruled "every host VAS we create". Commit 09252909 (2026-09-25) implemented it, because a space's kernel/user status is unknown when its mirror (or a prewarmed spare) is built. UVM's space only becomes kernel at its first Translated birth. The ruling was a convenience, not a functional need.

Nothing later removes, shrinks or protects the windows in user spaces. The v3-roperm kernel/user flag (efce970b, 2026-09-26) only gates privileged-leaf mirroring. Retired spaces keep their windows as spares for the next key. No commit on origin/master since 2026-09-29 touches the window code, and every v3 and security branch still has the 4 map_window calls.

Measured in a stock-driver fat guest (traces/v3_display/gop_box_20261003/run_b3_qemu.log, kf3 8c86c94a, same window code as master):
- Guest USER-privilege passthrough twins on GR and CE are born in spaces logged with both windows.
- In that boot, user twins withheld 8817 privileged guest leaves (0x4ce3d8000 bytes) while carrying the RW whole-object alias that backs them.
- Each fresh mirror paid ~315-320 ms for its RAM window.

Not measured: actual GPU reachability from a user twin. T-WINDOW-USER has never run, and that claim is UNVERIFIED.

VasKey is one mirror per guest VA-space OBJECT ((hClient<<32)|hVASpace, with dups folded to the original), not one per process.

result.summary:
Short answer: passing apps show that the mappings apps need are present. They cannot show that unneeded mappings are absent, and in the 61/65 run the two windows were present in the apps' own twin spaces.

Read at kayfabe origin/master e4fb0190. Measured evidence comes from traces/v3_cdp/app_matrix_2830988f/ (kf3 2830988f, which has the same window code at mem.rs:1724-1731).

A passthrough twin's host VA space holds two different kinds of mapping:

1. **Guest rows.** This is the part the owner's intuition is right about. The walker reads the guest's own page tables. For each leaf, the VA manager issues one fixed map at the guest's own VA, of a slice of the store or of the guest-RAM object. It refuses or withholds anything the guest did not ask for: guest-privileged leaves are withheld from user twins, and a leaf that overlaps a kayfabe placement is refused. Apps work because of these rows. Measured: privileged leaves were withheld in graphics, video and OpenCL apps (up to 130 427), and those apps still passed. `vmm_overlaps=0` in all 71 per-app logs.

2. **The two windows.** These are added by kayfabe, not by the guest. `create_mirror` maps the whole store (all guest VRAM, including the guest kernel's GPU page tables) and the whole guest-RAM object into every mirrored space. It does this whether the space is a user space or a kernel space. Spares and recycled spaces carry the windows too. The mapping is read-write and carries no privilege attribute: NVOS46 has no privilege field, and RM sets the PTE PRIV bit only for its own GR context buffers.

result.summary:
Short answer to the owner: you are right that v3 maps only what is needed, but that is true of the guest's own rows. It is not true of the two identity windows, and the 61/65 result cannot tell the difference.

**What v3 maps for an app's own process.** It maps only what the guest's page tables say. The walk and reconcile place guest rows, privileged guest leaves are withheld in user twins, and any guest row that overlaps a kayfabe placement is refused. Those rows are what the apps exercise.

**The windows are a separate thing kayfabe adds.** Each window is one mapping over a whole kayfabe-owned object: the store window covers all guest VRAM and the RAM window covers all guest RAM. They are placed when a mirror is created (and in prewarmed spares), not derived from any guest page-table entry.
- They are needed only by Translated channels, which run the guest kernel's own GPU work (RM's CeUtils and UVM). The rewriter turns their physical-address operands into window addresses.
- Passthrough twins, where an app's own channels run, never use them.
- They are in every space because THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE §12 chose that. A UVM space is only recognised as a kernel space when its first Translated channel is born, which happens after its mirror and spare already exist.

**Why the apps still pass with the windows present.**
- The windows sit at the top of the host VA space (GROWS_DOWN), above the 2^47 ceiling that guest allocations stay under, and any guest row overlapping them is refused. So a correct app never uses a window address, and the windows neither help nor disturb it.
- This was measured in the 61/65 run itself (kf3 2830988f). A guest user process's mirror (client 0xc1d00020) logged both windows: 8 GiB store and 16 GiB RAM, at the top of the 49-bit space. Passthrough twins were born in that same space, and deviceQuery passed. In the same log, RM/UVM's space became a guest-KERNEL space, which is where the windows are actually used.
- So 61/65 shows that everything an app uses is mapped correctly. It says nothing about whether extra memory is also mapped. The app matrix cannot detect this gap.

**Reachability, read from source (never measured).**
- The window mappings are read-write. They are not privileged: the map call (NVOS46) has no privilege flag, and in ogkm-580 RM's map path for it the privilege variable is zeroed and never set, so the page-table entry is written as non-privileged.
- A non-privileged entry is exactly what every ordinary CUDA allocation uses. The GPU's privilege fault fires only when a non-privileged access hits a privileged entry.
- So the P0 fix (twin channels born USER) does not reduce what the windows expose. P0 is measured on `v3-sec-nonpriv`, which is not yet merged into master.
- The windows lie within the address width of the copy-engine and compute inline-write operands (49-bit on GA10x). They lie above the 40-bit width of host semaphores and ring entries.
- Neither host RM nor the guest's own page tables limit the windows. kayfabe copies the guest's "privileged" marking only onto guest rows, and the windows bypass it by mapping the same memory without it.

**Measurement status.** T-WINDOW-USER, the test that would check reachability from a user twin, exists only in the audit text. No trace on any origin branch has run it.

**Two citation problems.**
- S1-21's line pointer is stale. The code is now at `kf-qemu/src/mem.rs:1786-1795`, and `prewarm` at `:1915-1921` also maps both windows.
- A source comment in kayfabe (kf-host `channel.rs:1104-1105`) cites the wrong ogkm function for where page-table privilege comes from. Its conclusion, that a client cannot set the bit, still holds.

Nothing was edited, committed or run on a box. Logs were extracted only to the scratchpad (`/tmp/claude-0/-workspace-nvidia-gpu-passthrough/85f9c0ab-d91a-47ab-b068-c099d453dd8f/scratchpad/am/`).

I tried every refutation angle I was given. None holds.

(a) Privileged bit. The windows go through NV_ESC_RM_MAP_MEMORY_DMA, then virtmemMapTo, dmaAllocMap and dmaAllocMapping_GM107. In that function pLocals->priv is never assigned. It is zeroed by portMemSet at virt_mem_allocator_gm107.c:404 and passed at :1500. :2233 therefore gives NV_MMU_PTE_PRIVILEGE_FALSE (VER2 field at :2515), and VER3 sets PCF REGULAR at :2460. In open RM the only producer of DMA_UPDATE_VASPACE_FLAGS_PRIV is dmaMapBuffer_GM107 (:2849-2850), RM's internal buffer path, which the windows do not use. NVOS46 has no privilege field at all (nvos.h:1974-2151). kayfabe's own code says the same thing (apply.rs:40-44, :241).

(b) Read-only or no-access. map_window passes only GROWS_DOWN (channel.rs:383-389). The choke point adds only page size (0 when not FIXED) and CACHE_SNOOP (kf-host/src/lib.rs:229-238). ACCESS and SHADER_ACCESS are both 0, i.e. READ_WRITE / DEFAULT (nvos.h:1975, :2009).

(c) Aperture. The store window is vidmem, mapped as GMMU_APERTURE_VIDEO (gm107.c:1197-1210). The RAM window is snooped sysmem, mapped as SYS_COH (:1340-1350). These are the same objects and apertures the user twins' own rows use: store slices, guest-RAM USERD and notifiers (chan.rs:2742-2798).

(d) Different VA space. Twins are born in the mirror's host space: the mirror is looked up by VasKey (chan.rs:2705-2712) and birth_group passes h_va_space = space.space (channel.rs:554-561). Twin work is submitted unparsed (THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE §4, §27), so guest-authored virtual operands are translated through that space's page tables, windows included.

(e) Windows only in kernel spaces. Not so. The §12 design rule is literally "it goes in every host VAS we create". kernel_vas only gates guest privileged leaves (mem.rs:921-928), and no code removes windows from a user space.

On the owner's question: "only map what's needed" is true of the rows, and is not true of the windows. The windows exist for the Translated plane: Windows/SlotWindow (chan.rs:491-523) is used only by the Translated slot pump (chan.rs:3380). Passthrough twins never use them; the P1+P2 design says the same.

61/65 apps passing measures completeness: no needed mapping is missing. It does not measure minimality: no extra mapping is present. The windows sit GROWS_DOWN above the guest's reserved allocatable ranges (§24.2; channel.rs GUEST_VA_RANGES), so they neither collide with app VAs nor get named by them. The app-matrix run at 2830988f itself shows a user mirror created with both windows and CUDA's passthrough GR twins born in that same space.

The finding is a READ conclusion backed by measured presence of the windows. The end-to-end access test (T-WINDOW-USER) has not run.

result.reasoning:
I tried to refute S1-21 from three directions and none worked.

(A) Are the windows actually in user twin spaces? Yes. create_mirror runs for every VasKey a page-directory statement names, with no kernel/user branch. It maps the store window and the RAM window unconditionally. Passthrough user channels are born in mirror.space, the same host space. So guest user GPU work runs in a host space that holds both windows.

(B) Are the windows outside what a user-driven engine can translate? I found nothing that limits them. Placement is the host RM's choice in the twin space. The guest kernel's own VA limit only governs the guest's allocator; the hardware walks the twin's page tables, not the guest's. No code path restricts which channels in a space can translate through the windows. The only per-mirror privilege control in the tree, withholds_privileged, applies to mirrored guest leaves and not to the windows. I stop at the property level and do not describe naming or access.

(C) Is the impact overstated? Not materially. The identity window's length is the guest FB layout's fb_length, which is the store length. The RAM object is an OS descriptor over the whole guest memfd. The design doc records the walker reading the guest's page tables in place through the window. Guest page tables in sysmem would fall under the RAM window instead.

On the owner's question about 61 apps: passing apps cannot refute this. Mapping too much never makes an app fail; only mapping too little does. The apps pass because the guest's own rows are mirrored correctly. The windows are additional mappings that exist for Translated (kernel) channels and kayfabe's own reads. So 'v3 maps only what is needed' is true of the mirrored guest rows and false of the windows.

Weak points: the 'no privileged flag' wording names a mechanism that may not be selectable from userspace RM. The cited line numbers have moved. Reachability is READ, not MEASURED.
